
# Scoreboard Challenge

![Server-Side-Vulnerabilities/Access-control/Score-board Challenge 20260926-054740.png|579](data:image/png;base64,)

Now this challenge forms a series of challenges I'll be tackling from the famous OWASP Juice Shop.
The first challenge despite the fact being dubbed easy after scouring through a lot of pages on devtools I can confidently it wasnot quite easy,so yeah maybe it was easy to you.So lets get at it !

First of all I used the dev tools to try and find the anything from the files alloys available when you access it but nothing of much importance came by so I decided to pivot to something else,
Directory brute force using tools like `ffuf` and `gobuster` none of this tools proved otherwise 

So I did what any attacker would do in a desperate situation and that is to test the path manually,so As much as I did it manually it wasn't some random guesses.
From my earlier brute-force I had come up with a word list variants so as to speed up the process which I used as reference 

```
#A simple program to compute the variants of scoreboard

score = "scoreboard"
variants = [
    score,
    score.lower(),
    score.upper(),
    score.capitalize(),
    score.replace("o", ""),
    score.replace("e", ""),
    score.replace("a", ""),
    score.replace("score", "Score"),
    score.replace("board", "Board"),
    "score_board",
    "score-board",
    "ScoreBoard",
    "Score_Board",
]

with open("variants.txt", "w") as f:
    for v in set(variants):
        f.write(v + "\n")
```

Run the program and we get the different naming convention a developer can use to name the path pointing to our scoreboard.
As shown below:

```
The variants get saved in a file called variants.txt

SCOREBOARD
screbard
Scoreboard
scoreBoard
score-board
Score_Board
scorebord
ScoreBoard
scoreboard
scorboard
score_board
```
